text:
These days, I believe polyamory is often a way to cope with an inability to connect deeply with one person, or a way to admit a lack of self-control without necessarily doing the self-development that would make the arrangement ethical.

That doesn't describe everyone doing polyamory. If you can't do monogamy, it's still better to say that than promise it.

A lot of monogamous couples seem to be doing something stranger: both people know more than they're allowed to say. One notices somebody else. Feelings change. Jealousy starts turning into possession. Now even talking about it threatens the agreement. Sometimes hiding all that does more damage than the outside connection would have.

Love is real. The form built around it can still be broken. A foundational, permanent, exclusive romantic partnership is promised far more often than it is actually lived.
